title: Cold rebuild: damage and levels
summary: Write Damage, Level and XpToNext again from memory. Proves the module before its boss.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: No starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. You wrote this piece earlier in the module; now write it again **from memory**, against the same checks.

This is how a skill sticks: getting it back out of your head after a few days, not reading it again. If you get stuck, that is useful information: go back to the lesson, then come back here and try again with an empty editor.
Passing it marks the piece as **proven** in your Delve build.

steps.title: Cold rebuild: damage and levels
prompt: From memory, the three functions from **Whole numbers and fractions**, with the same names and the same checks. No `if`, no `?`.
- `static int Damage(int attack, int armour)`: armour blocks one point per full three points of attack, at most its own size. `Damage(9, 5)` is 6, `Damage(9, 1)` is 8.
- `static int Level(int xp)`: a level per 50 xp, from level 1.
- `static int XpToNext(int xp)`: xp still needed for the next level.
steps.starter: // From memory: no starter, no hints.
solution: static int Damage(int attack, int armour)
template: Dojo.Eq("Damage(9, 5) blocks three full threes", 6, Damage(9, 5));
Dojo.Eq("Damage(9, 1): armour blocks no more than it has", 8, Damage(9, 1));
Dojo.Eq("Damage(2, 4): a weak hit still lands", 2, Damage(2, 4));

forbid.message: Every function starts with `static` (Delve keeps its pieces in one static class)
